;Business and economy
*[[Coronavirus recession]], [[Immigration to the United States]]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] suspends the entry of some [[Skilled worker|skilled]] and seasonal workers entering the [[United States]], claiming it will open jobs to citizens. Business groups criticize this move as stifling economic recovery. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-immigration-workers/trump-suspends-entry-of-certain-foreign-workers-despite-business-opposition-idUSKBN23T2ZW (Reuters)]

;International relations
*[[India–Nepal relations]]
**Nepalese authorities stop officials of the Water Resources Department of the [[Government of Bihar|Bihar government]] from carrying out infrastructural maintenance work in Indian territory along the [[India–Nepal border]], claiming the area as part of its territory. The incident comes four days after the lower house of the [[Federal Parliament of Nepal|Nepalese parliament]] approved a new map of the country that included Indian territory in the Indian state of [[Uttarakhand]]. [https://m.timesofindia.com/india/nepal-obstructing-bihar-govt-from-flood-prevention-related-work-bihar-minister-says-will-approach-mea/amp_articleshow/76507256.cms (''Times of India'')]
*[[China–United States relations]]
**The [[United States Department of State|U.S. State Department]] adds four [[Mass media in China|Chinese media organizations]], including the [[public broadcasting]] service [[China Central Television]], to its list of organizations participating in "foreign missions" due to their connections with the ruling [[Communist Party of China|Communist Party]]. They will be required to report all their employees and any real estate holdings to the American government. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/restrict-chinese-media-outlets-deemed-propaganda-200622220638775.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[China]] announces its decision to join the [[United Nations]] [[Arms Trade Treaty]]. [https://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2020/06/22/china-to-join-un-arms-trade-treaty-enhance-world-peace.html (AFP via ''The Jakarta Post'')]
*Thousands of [[Palestinians]] and dozens of foreign diplomats attend a rally in [[Jericho]] to oppose [[Israel]]'s plan to unilaterally [[Annexation of the Jordan Valley|annex the Jordan Valley]] and [[Israeli settlement|the settlements]] in the [[Israeli occupation of the West Bank|occupied West Bank]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/thousands-palestinians-protest-israeli-annexation-plan-200622173919963.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Law and crime
*A police officer of the [[New York City Police Department]] is suspended without pay after he is captured on camera using a [[chokehold]] against a 35-year-old man in [[Queens]].  The use of chokeholds by police was recently banned, both in [[New York City]] and the [[New York (state)|state of New York]]. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/nypd-ricky-bellevue-chokehold-cop-suspended-police-officer-a9579661.html?utm_term=Autofeed&utm_medium=Social&utm_source=Twitter&amp=1#Echobox=1592845009 (''The Independent'')]
*Two suspects are arrested in [[Oregon]] in connection to a [[mass shooting]] at a residence in [[Valhermoso Springs, Alabama]], on June 4 that killed seven people. [https://www.wbrc.com/2020/06/22/morgan-county-authorities-fbi-updating-public-septuple-homicide/ (WBRC)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Kiribati presidential election]]
**Citizens in [[Kiribati]] head to the polls to elect their [[President of Kiribati|President]]. The main issue of the election is whether to maintain relations with [[China]] or [[Taiwan]]. Incumbent [[Taneti Maamau]], who switched recognition from Taiwan to China last year, is facing candidate [[Banuera Berina]] who favors re-establishing relations with Taiwan. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/419528/kiribati-to-hold-presidential-election-today (RNZ)]

;Science and technology
*[[Apple's transition to ARM processors]]
**[[Apple Inc.]] announces a transition of its personal computer products from using [[Intel]] processors to using [[ARM architecture|ARM]]-based processors designed by Apple. Since 2006, the company has used Intel processors in its computer offerings. [https://www.theverge.com/2020/6/22/21295475/apple-mac-processors-arm-silicon-chips-wwdc-2020 (''The Verge'')]

;Sports
*[[2020 NASCAR Cup Series]]
**[[George Floyd protests#Sports industry|George Floyd protests § Sports industry]]
***[[NASCAR]] launches an investigation after a [[noose]] was found in the garage area of [[Bubba Wallace]], the lone African-American driver in the series, at [[Talladega Superspeedway]], in [[Talladega, Alabama]], vowing to "eliminate [those responsible] from the sport". Wallace had recently successfully pushed NASCAR to enforce a five-year-old ban on the [[Confederate battle flag|Confederate flag]] being [[Modern display of the Confederate battle flag|displayed]] at its race tracks and properties. A plane pulling a banner with a Confederate flag and the phrase "Defund NASCAR" flew over the race track on June 21. [https://www.ctvnews.ca/sports/nascar-noose-found-in-bubba-wallace-garage-at-alabama-race-1.4994036 (CTV News)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-53132933 (BBC News)]
***The [[United States Department of Justice]] and [[Federal Bureau of Investigation]] launch their own investigations in order to determine whether criminal charges can be brought. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nascar/2020/06/22/justice-department-fbi-investigate-noose-bubba-wallaces-garage/3235453001/ (''USA Today'')]
